title: XGrammar: Flexible and Efficient Structured Generation Engine for Large Language Models
problem: Context-free grammar (CFG) constrained decoding for LLMs is slow because every token generation step requires recomputing token masks from scratch, dominating inference latency for structured output generation.
method: XGrammar splits the token vocabulary into context-independent tokens (whose acceptance can be precomputed offline once per grammar) and context-dependent tokens (requiring runtime evaluation). For Llama-3.1 with JSON grammar, only 1,134 of 128k tokens are context-dependent (<1%). A persistent pushdown automaton stack tracks parser state. Context expansion reduces context-dependent tokens further (to ~120, a 90% reduction). An adaptive token mask cache stores masks per parser state, with 0.2% memory overhead. CPU-GPU overlap hides remaining mask computation behind GPU attention.

title: No Rush in Executing Atomic Instructions
problem: Modern x86 processors implement unfenced atomic RMW instructions (no implicit serializing fences), enabling eager execution as soon as operands are ready, but eager execution locks cachelines early which prolongs the lock duration and harms other threads attempting to acquire the same contended cacheline. Conversely, lazy execution (waiting until the atomic is oldest in the load queue and the store buffer is empty) minimizes cacheline lock time but exposes full memory access latency on non-contended accesses.
method: Rush or Wait (RoW) is a hardware mechanism that dynamically selects between eager and lazy atomic execution via a 64-entry, 4-bit saturating-counter contention predictor indexed by the XOR of the 12 least-significant PC bits. At issue, the predictor determines the execution mode; at completion, it updates using three progressively refined contention detection mechanisms: (1) Execution Window (EW) — marks an atomic contended if an external coherence invalidation/downgrade arrives while the cacheline is locked; (2) Ready Window (RW) — extends tracking to the window from when the atomic's operands are ready by computing the address eagerly and snooping the Atomic Queue (AQ) for address matches on external requests; (3) Directory detection (RW+Dir) — additionally marks an atomic contended when the cacheline arrives from another core's private cache with latency exceeding a 400-cycle threshold, catching cases where contention is resolved before an external request reaches the core. Store-to-load forwarding from older regular stores overrides a lazy prediction to improve atomic locality. Total storage: 64 bytes (256-bit predictor + 256-bit AQ augmentation).

title: NEO: Saving GPU Memory Crisis with CPU Offloading for Online LLM Inference
problem: GPU memory limits LLM inference batch size, wasting GPU compute; existing CPU offloading systems either hurt latency (symmetric pipelining bubbles) or require expensive dedicated CPUs.
method: NEO asymmetric GPU-CPU pipelining: each iteration splits into two sub-batches. Batch-0 (all prefill requests + most decode requests) runs a long linear projection stage on GPU. Batch-1 (CPU-assigned decode requests) runs a long attention stage on CPU — both overlap. KV cache split into GPU-cache (HBM) and CPU-cache (DRAM). Layer-wise KV swap overlaps PCIe transfer with GPU compute. Load-aware scheduler uses offline-profiled time models + linear interpolation to greedily assign requests per iteration, comparing GPU-only vs asymmetric pipelining and choosing higher throughput. ISPC-compiled SPMD CPU attention kernels (PACPU) with paged attention, SIMD loads, and Flash Decoding-style parallelism across cores.

title: Self-Data Distillation for Recovering Quality in Pruned Large Language Models
problem: Structured depth pruning of LLMs removes decoder blocks and reduces compute, but post-pruning SFT causes catastrophic forgetting by shifting the data distribution away from the original model's knowledge.
method: Angular cosine distance between adjacent block outputs is used to identify which layers are most redundant (lowest angular distance = most similar outputs = best pruning candidates). The unpruned model then rewrites the fine-tuning dataset: for each prompt, the unpruned model generates a 'distilled' response that preserves semantic richness. Conditional selection keeps original responses for prompts where the pruned model already performs acceptably. SLERP model merging blends pruned and distilled model checkpoints. The pruned model is also used as a speculative decoding draft model paired with the full model as verifier.

title: FlashInfer: Efficient and Customizable Attention Engine for LLM Inference Serving
problem: LLM inference serving requires attention kernels that simultaneously handle heterogeneous KV-cache storage layouts (ragged, paged, tree-structured), diverse attention variants (GQA, MLA, sliding-window), and dynamic request batching, while remaining compatible with static CUDAGraph capture.
method: FlashInfer introduces: (1) Block-Sparse Row (BSR) format as a unified KV-cache representation that encodes ragged, paged, and prefix-tree layouts via a single sparse block structure; (2) composable format decomposition that splits shared-prefix attention from unique-suffix attention and merges partial softmax accumulators; (3) a JIT compiler that instantiates CUDA attention templates per attention variant at first use, reusing compiled binaries across requests; (4) a load-balanced scheduler that uses a priority queue to assign work tiles to thread blocks while preserving CUDAGraph compatibility via a static wrapper that hides dynamic dispatch.
